en.title: Street Fighter Movie's Mixed Reviews Hint at a Messy Bout
en.summary: The latest live-action adaptation of the iconic fighting game series has landed in theaters, and critics are divided. While the film has made a notable splash at the box office, its reception among reviewers is far from a knockout.
en.body:
The roar of the crowd and the clang of fists have returned to the big screen with the new **Street Fighter** movie, released last week. Directed by **Kitao Sakurai** and co-written by **Sakurai** and **T. J. Fixman**, this marks the third major live-action cinematic outing for Capcom’s legendary fighting game franchise. Early box office reports indicate a strong opening weekend, with the film reportedly grossing $51.1 million globally, though this figure falls slightly short of the recent **Mortal Kombat 2** movie's debut. The ensemble cast features a diverse lineup, including **Noah Centineo**, **Andrew Koji**, **Callina Liang**, and wrestling superstar **Joe "Roman Reigns" Anoa'i**, alongside actors like **David Dastmalchian**, **Cody Rhodes**, and **Don Lee**.

## The Critics' Corner: A Flurry of Opinions

Reviews for **Street Fighter** are proving to be as varied as the characters in the game's roster. While many critics acknowledge the effort put into the fight choreography, praising its energy and visual flair, a common point of contention is the film's narrative coherence. Some reviews, like those highlighted by Happy Console Gamer, note that the action sequences are solid but are hampered by shaky camera work that detracts from the impact. The esteemed **Roger Ebert**’s review, for instance, points out that while the film delivers on action, it struggles to weave a compelling and cohesive story. PC Gamer's analysis paints a picture of a film that isn't a complete disaster but is undeniably a "mess," suggesting a general disappointment among the critical community. The film carries a PG-13 rating, accommodating a runtime of 2 hours and 5 minutes, indicating an ambitious scope that reviewers feel the storytelling didn't quite match.

## Fan Anticipation vs. Critical Consensus

For fans who have followed the **Street Fighter** saga for decades, the release of a new movie is always a significant event. The franchise boasts a rich history, from its groundbreaking arcade origins to its enduring presence in esports and pop culture. The hope is always for an adaptation that captures the spirit and excitement of the games while offering a fresh, engaging cinematic experience. However, the current critical reception suggests that this iteration may have stumbled in translating its impressive fight sequences into a satisfying narrative. The mixed reviews leave fans wondering if this film will resonate as a worthy addition to the **Street Fighter** legacy or become another cautionary tale in the often-treacherous landscape of video game adaptations.

## What's Next for the Franchise

With the film now in theaters, the focus will shift to its box office performance over the coming weeks and how it fares with general audiences. Further critical analyses and audience scores will continue to roll in, providing a clearer picture of its overall success. Details regarding potential sequels or future **Street Fighter** projects have not yet been announced.
